title: Days, months and dates
goal: Name the days and months, say and ask today's date, and read dates the way they are written in France and Canada.

items.fr: lundi, mardi, mercredi, jeudi, vendredi, samedi, dimanche

drills.explain: The week starts on lundi: lundi, mardi, mercredi, jeudi…

drills.prompt: Which spelling is correct in a French sentence?
drills.explain: No capital letter for months, and no de between the number and the month.
décembre, with é and no capital letter.

items.en: saying a date: le 3 mars, le premier mai

drills.explain: Only the 1st uses premier. All other days use the normal number: le 2 mai, le 3 mai…
le + number + month. And no l' before huit: le huit mars.

drills.prompt: How do you say “on the 11th of July”?
drills.explain: Use the normal number, and never l' before onze or huit.

items.note: Say “yair” (some people say “ee-yair”). You will use it in sentences when you learn the past tense.

example.fr: L'anniversaire de Camille, c'est le 29 avril.

blocks.title: A notice at a community centre in Gatineau
blocks.fr:
Cours de français pour les nouveaux arrivants
Le cours commence le lundi 14 septembre 2026.

blocks.en:
French classes for newcomers
The course starts on Monday, September 14, 2026.

blocks.body: New chunks to understand: [[c'est quand ?]] = when is it?, [[ton anniversaire]] = your birthday (to a friend), [[mon anniversaire]] = my birthday, [[le dernier cours]] = the last class.

blocks.title: Les jours de la semaine (the days of the week)
head: English
French
blocks.note: The French week starts on **Monday**. Days are masculine and take **no capital letter**.

blocks.title: Les mois (the months)
head: English
French
English
French
blocks.note: Months are masculine and also take **no capital letter**: [[en mars]], [[le 3 mars]]. You may see [[aout]] without the circumflex: that newer spelling is accepted too.

blocks.title: Saying a date
blocks.note: French uses the **normal number**, not “third” or “fourth”, and **no “of”**. The only exception is the 1st: [[le premier]] (written **1er**). Put the article [[le]] before the number, even with a day name: [[le lundi 14 septembre]].

examples.fr: le huit août deux mille vingt-six

blocks.title: Asking and giving today's date
blocks.body:
Two ways to ask:

- [[Quelle est la date aujourd'hui ?]] (neutral, fine everywhere)
- [[On est le combien aujourd'hui ?]] (very common in conversation; literally “we are the how-many?”)

To answer, use [[on est]] or [[nous sommes]] (être, from Unit 2), or [[c'est]]:

- [[On est le trois mars.]] / [[Nous sommes le trois mars.]]
- [[Aujourd'hui, c'est lundi.]] / [[Demain, c'est mardi.]]

[[Hier]] means *yesterday*. For now, just learn the word; you will use it in full sentences with the past tense in A2.

blocks.title: Years
blocks.body:
Years from 2000 start with [[deux mille]] (two thousand). [[Mille]] never takes an *s*: [[deux mille vingt-six]] = 2026, [[deux mille trente]] = 2030.

You will also hear older years, like birth years. Just recognize them for now: 1990 = [[mille neuf cent quatre-vingt-dix]], literally “thousand nine hundred ninety”. In Québec you will also often hear [[dix-neuf cent quatre-vingt-dix]] (“nineteen hundred ninety”). To say “in 2026”, use [[en]]: [[en deux mille vingt-six]].

- **Capitals:** [[le lundi 3 Mars]] is wrong. Write [[le lundi 3 mars]]. Days and months take a capital only at the start of a sentence.
- **No “of”:** not [[le 3 de mars]], just [[le 3 mars]].
- **No ordinals except 1st:** not [[le troisième mars]], just [[le trois mars]]. But [[le premier mai]], never [[le un mai]].
- **No élision before huit and onze:** [[le huit mars]], [[le onze juillet]], not [[l'huit]] or [[l'onze]].
- **Juin / juillet:** [[juin]] is one short syllable with a nasal vowel; [[juillet]] is two syllables, “jwee-yeh”.

- [[mars]]: you hear the *s*.
- [[août]]: you will hear both “oo” and “oot” (“oot” is very common in Québec). Both are correct.
- [[septembre]]: the *p* is pronounced here, unlike in [[sept]].
- [[mois]]: “mwa”, silent *s*.
- [[aujourd'hui]]: “o-joor-dwee”, three short syllables.

blocks.title: Writing dates in Canada
blocks.body:
In France, dates are written **day / month / year**: **28/04/2026**. In the US, **month / day / year**: 04/28/2026. Canada uses both, which can be confusing! Is **03/04/2026** March 4 or April 3?

That is why the international format **year-month-day** is often recommended in Canada and Québec: **2026-04-28**. On Québec forms you will often see the letters **AAAA-MM-JJ**: **a**nnée (year), **m**ois (month), **j**our (day). Always check which format a form asks for.

Two dates to know: [[le premier juillet]] is Canada Day, and in Québec it is also the traditional moving day, when many leases end. [[Le vingt-quatre juin]] is the Fête nationale du Québec. And in Québec, the weekend is often [[la fin de semaine]] instead of [[le week-end]].

blocks.title: Listen and repeat
blocks.note: Repeat the days, then the months, then the dates.

janvier, février, mars, avril, mai, juin
juillet, août, septembre, octobre, novembre, décembre

lines.tip: In dates, you usually hear the t: “luh weet mars”.

blocks.explain: [[premier]] = 1st, and [[mai]] = May. March is [[mars]], with an s.
[[juillet]] has two syllables; [[juin]] has one. And [[onze]] = 11.
No l' before huit, and no capital on mars. Digits are fine for the number.
The 1st is [[premier]], written 1er. [[Août]] keeps its circumflex in traditional spelling.

blocks.prompt: How do you write “July 4” in French?
blocks.explain: le + normal number + month, no capital.
optionFeedback: Months take no capital letter in French.
French uses the normal number, except for the 1st.
There is no de between the number and the month.

blocks.explain: [[Aujourd'hui, c'est…]] or [[On est…]], with no capital on vendredi.
[[Quelle est la date aujourd'hui ?]] works everywhere; [[On est le combien ?]] is very common in speech.

blocks.fr: L'anniversaire de Lucie, c'est le vingt-quatre juin.
blocks.explain: [[vingt-quatre]] = 24 and [[juin]] = June. June 24 is also the Fête nationale du Québec!

blocks.prompt: A Québec form asks for your date of birth as AAAA-MM-JJ. You were born on March 9, 1995. What do you write?
blocks.explain: AAAA = année (year), MM = mois (month), JJ = jour (day): year first, then month, then day.

blocks.en: On March 3, we are in Toronto.

blocks.prompt: Say today's date (day, number, month, year), what day it is tomorrow, and the date of your birthday.

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: Aujourd'hui, on est samedi, le dix-sept octobre deux mille vingt-six. Demain, c'est dimanche. Mon anniversaire, c'est le premier février.
models.en: Today is Saturday, October 17, 2026. Tomorrow is Sunday. My birthday is February 1st.

blocks.prompt: Write a short message to a new friend: give today's date, the date of your birthday, and the days of your French class.
checklist: Today's date with le + number + month
No capital letters on days and months

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: Salut Alex ! Aujourd'hui, c'est le 2 mars. Mon anniversaire, c'est le 12 mars ! Le cours de français est le mardi et le jeudi.
models.en: Hi Alex! Today is March 2. My birthday is March 12! The French class is on Tuesdays and Thursdays.

summary:
- Name the days ([[lundi]]…[[dimanche]]) and months ([[janvier]]…[[décembre]]), without capitals
- Say a date: [[le trois mars]], [[le premier mai]], [[deux mille vingt-six]]
- Ask [[Quelle est la date aujourd'hui ?]] / [[On est le combien ?]] and answer [[On est le…]]
- Use [[aujourd'hui]], [[demain]] and recognize [[hier]]; read Canadian dates in AAAA-MM-JJ format
